sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Localization assay in transfected cells: surface display confirmed; GPI anchoring preserved (construct described as 'able to produce the mature GPI-anchored CD24'). C-terminal FLAG comparator lost GPI anchoring, validating the N-terminal junction as functionally silent.
sites.rationale: The signal peptide spans residues 1–26 (authoritative landmark); 'after the ER-signal sequence' unambiguously places the tag between residue 26 (S) and residue 27 (S), the mature N-terminus. Python confirmed residue_before = S (pos 26) and residue_after = S (pos 27). CD24 is GPI-anchored with no TM helix and no cytoplasmic domain, so this terminus is fully extracellular and the only surface-accessible terminus available for a tag that must survive signal-peptide cleavage. Full-length CD24 construct with DDK-FLAG inserted explicitly 'after the ER-signal sequence' (signal peptide 1–26), producing a GPI-anchored, surface-displayed protein in transiently transfected cells. The paper explicitly contrasts this with a C-terminal FLAG version that disrupts GPI anchoring, confirming the N-terminal junction is the functional one.

sources.claim: The localization of CD24 was investigated by transient transfection with two different plasmid constructs (as illustrated in Figure 2 ); one with the DDK-flag sequence inserted after the ER-signal sequence, able to produce the mature GPI-anchored CD24 (ER-tag CD24) and the other, not able to produce a GPI-anchor-modified CD24 due to the biochemical alteration of the GPI-anchor signal milieu by the presence of the acidic DDK-flag sequence inserted at the C-terminal of CD24 [ 46 ] (GPI-tag CD24).

Cluster of differentiation 24 (CD24), a glycoprotein contain two N-glycosylation sites and anchors to glycosyl-phosphatidyl-inositol (GPI), 17 we first fused CD24 with enhanced green fluorescent protein (eGFP) at the N-terminus as a tag for targeting.

literature_notes: CD24 (80 aa) is a GPI-anchored protein with signal peptide 1–26 and a single extracellular domain 27–80; it has no TM helix and no cytoplasmic tail. The only extracellular terminus available for a surface tag that survives signal-peptide cleavage is the mature N-terminus (after residue 26). L1 explicitly validates this junction with a DDK-FLAG tag in a full-length, GPI-anchored, surface-displayed construct. L2/L3 independently validate the same junction with eGFP by topology derivation (surface display confirmed, no residue named). The C-terminal FLAG from L1 is recorded in other_positions because it disrupts GPI anchoring. No internal loop insertions are supported by the ledger.

literature_other_positions.note: DDK-FLAG inserted at the C-terminus of full-length CD24 disrupted GPI anchoring, preventing surface display of the mature GPI-anchored form.
